title: The AI Bubble: Why Being Right About the Tech Means Being Wrong About the Stock
speaker: Kevin Muir (guest), host Ilya Spivak

macro_themes.view: AI is a bubble of dot-com proportions; transformative technologies attract over-investment and end up poor investments.
Hyperscalers have gone from buybacks to record debt and equity issuance as free cash flow turns negative, removing a key bull tailwind.
Everyone (US, Canada, Germany, Japan) is now running hot fiscal policy, pushing real long-term yields higher.
Bonds breaking will break equities until equities breaking saves bonds; when the AI trade cracks, money rotates into long bonds.

macro_themes.theme: US more at risk than China
macro_themes.view: US economy depends on the stock-market bubble and record deficits; China is deliberately running slow and has the savings to stimulate later.

calls.instrument_quoted: Nasdaq / AI and Mag 7 stocks (no prices)
calls.reason: AI capex is debt- and equity-funded with negative free cash flow, earnings are pulled forward from hyperscaler spending, and over-investment always ends badly; higher rates are choking the real economy leaving only the bubble.
calls.quote: This is a bubble of dot proportions.

calls.condition: If stocks stop going up / the AI trade comes unglued, money rotates into bonds; he still half-expects a final puke lower in bonds first
calls.reason: Has taken stabs long bonds; pensions fully funded, bearish Economist cover is contrarian, and stocks selling off while bonds rally on hot CPI may mark the return of negative correlation. Long run he fears a steepening.
calls.quote: I am no longer as bearish. Um I I I have taken stabs on the long side.

notes: Taped 'Wednesday', hot CPI day; Wednesday in that week is 2026-10-14 (listing said 10-15). Bond call recorded on TLT (bullish = yields down) rather than TNX/TYX to keep bias direction clear. Long-term bond bias 'mixed' because he calls himself a bond bear at heart and worries about curve steepening. Silver anecdote (bought 30, sold 60, went to 120) is past, not a call.
